candidate.title: Initiative
candidate.problemStatement: Lower-level direction, perspective, authority, and occurrence objects do not by themselves identify which Pursuits, participants, Assignments, decisions, and settlement state form one continuing coordinated software-work context.
candidate.scope: Accepted as a software-development Domain Profile Primitive under KFD-11; cross-domain vocabulary, historical novelty, universal minimum fields, and KFD-11 activation are not claimed.

observationPerspective.bearer: human and agent participants refining the software action substrate
observationPerspective.proximity: inside the implementation and contract boundary
consequences: bears API, storage, migration, verification, and responsibility-separation defects

genesis.observation: From the developer view, the natural continuation was finer control over action coordinates. Moving to the real user's consequence position exposed a different need: preserve one continuing body of coordinated work without making the user reconstruct it from coordinates and task records.
genesis.candidateObject: An Initiative is an independently addressable context that turns declared intent into continuing coordinated software work by preserving scope, participants, relevant Pursuits, Assignment relations, lineage, and settlement state.
genesis.claimBoundary: The cut accepts independent software-work responsibility, not a universal ontology, mandatory user-visible object, physical storage shape, or proof that Initiative is historically novel.

methodEvidence.observer: Kungfu Mission Control implementers and reviewers

transformedPerspective.bearer: a person using agents to advance consequential software work
transformedPerspective.proximity: inside continuity, coordination, handoff, and settlement consequences
consequences: bears repeated explanation, fragmented direction, responsibility drift, and unclear settlement

genesis.transformation: The observer moved from implementing independent action coordinates to the person responsible for making one continuing body of real work understandable and governable.
genesis.newlyVisibleNeed: A stable software-work context must coordinate multiple directions and bounded responsibilities without fusing their lower identities or requiring the user to operate the substrate directly.
genesis.methodNotes: The founding Mission vocabulary supplied first-party pressure; KFD-11 later assigned Initiative as the canonical software-profile term.

contactSides: independent action coordinates, tasks, sessions, and provider-local records
the person and agents continuing one coordinated body of software work
boundaryPressure.implicitHandling: Coordination is reconstructed from project prose, task grouping, chat memory, issue labels, branch names, and the maintainer's current understanding.

pressureChanges.description: Multiple humans and agents join, leave, and resume the same coordinated work.
One real initiative spans many Pursuits, Assignments, Episodes, repositories, and decisions.
Incorrect grouping changes priorities, handoff, settlement, and which work should continue together.

observedFailures: Lower-level objects remain individually valid while the continuing coordination context must be reconstructed.
Completing one task or Pursuit is mistaken for settling the larger work.
A new participant cannot tell which responsibilities belong to one coordinated effort.
boundaryPressure.mediationClaim: Initiative may preserve one continuing software-work context while referencing rather than absorbing Pursuit, Atlas, Warrant, Episode, and Assignment identities.
boundaryPressure.internalObjectAlternative: A disciplined project, workflow aggregate, or typed relation graph may implement equivalent Initiative semantics without using this name.

pressure: Real users need a stable work-level object rather than direct manipulation of action coordinates.
Long-running work spans several directions, participants, responsibilities, Episodes, and decisions.
Coordination and settlement state must survive sessions, agents, repositories, and mutable projections.
grounding.evidenceBoundary: Public KFD-11 and first-party Kungfu Mission Control implementation establish one software profile with stable work identity, lifecycle, queries, assessment, portability, and participant surfaces. No independent non-Kungfu implementation or universal domain transfer is included.
knownGaps: No independent adopter using the Initiative name
No proof that the current field set is globally minimal

alternatives.name: One Pursuit
alternatives.reason: A continuing direction does not by itself own the participant set, several Pursuits, Assignment relations, and work-level settlement state.

alternatives.name: Project, workflow, or issue aggregate
alternatives.reason: These may be valid Domain Profile implementations when they preserve equivalent identity, lineage, responsibility, and settlement semantics.

alternatives.name: More precise Atlas, Pursuit, and Warrant control
alternatives.reason: This remains necessary substrate work but does not remove the higher coordination responsibility unless equivalent grouping is added.

alternatives.name: No new Primitive
alternatives.reason: The deletion witness changes coordination and settlement decisions while lower object facts remain fixed.

contractModel.identity: A stable initiative_ref for one continuing coordinated body of software work.
contractModel.boundary: Declared intent, scope, participants, relevant Pursuit roots, Assignment relations, lineage, and settlement state; lower facts, authority, perspective, and occurrence remain references.
contractModel.authority: Initiative authority may declare and coordinate work but cannot manufacture facts, grant Warrant authority, prove occurrence, accept claims, or publish Project Cut settlement by itself.
contractModel.lifecycle: proposed -> active -> paused or revised -> settled, abandoned, superseded, or forked; exact state vocabulary remains Domain Profile-owned

minimumClosure.notes: Stable identity, declared intent and scope, relevant Pursuits, participants, Assignment relations, lineage, and settlement state are sufficient for the bounded software profile while lower authority remains external.

deletion.notes: Deleting Initiative while holding lower roots fixed changes which work and responsibilities must be coordinated and settled together.

fuse.notes: Fusing Initiative with Pursuit, repository, or project makes coordination scope and lower direction identity silently co-vary; equivalent typed relations remain allowed.

falsifiers: Initiative grouping is always derivable from lower roots with no reconstruction or changed decision.
Independent software workflows cannot map their project or work aggregate without forced semantics.
The minimum closure creates more coordination burden than it removes.
Progressive disclosure cannot preserve the simple-session experience.

dogfood.notes: The founding Mission profile exercised stable identity, fact admission, progress assessment, Cost/State/Proof, portability, and human/agent surfaces. The evidence is first-party and software-scoped.

decision.reason: Within the KFD-11 software profile, Initiative preserves a coordination and settlement distinction that changes required decisions when lower action coordinates remain fixed, and the first-party implementation demonstrates executable lifecycle and continuation value.
residualRisks: The object may map to an ordinary project or workflow aggregate in other products.
The founding evidence is correlated with one organization and product family.
The current minimum closure may narrow before KFD-11 activation.
Cross-domain use and historical novelty are unqualified.
